note: Skills that use the uidaho server's tools or the University of Idaho's own data: policy and rate lookups, a Rates sheet, the award skills that read Banner exports (FRIGITD, FRIPSTG), and the proposal workbook whose steps span the general, ai4ra and uidaho servers. Same shape as AI4RA/prompt-library's component_catalog.json, hand-maintained.

components.name: uidaho-lookup
components.summary: Answer a question about the University of Idaho's sponsored-research facts (F&A and fringe rates, budget rules, policies, contacts) with the uidaho tools, quoting each figure or passage with its policy number, effective period or revision date, and page.

components.name: uidaho-rates-sheet
components.summary: Write the University of Idaho's current F&A and fringe rates onto a sheet named Rates, read from the rate agreement and the fringe-rate page, one row per rate with its effective period and document, seven fixed-label rows a budget form reads first and a Source line for provenance.

components.name: award-facts
components.summary: Read an award's facts off the key block at the top of a Banner Grant Inception to Date export (FRIGITD), on the tab the request names, else the only tab that looks like the export, else the one the user is on, and says which: grant code, title, sponsor, PI, project start and end dates as written. Seven lines in the reply; nothing written.

components.name: award-lines
components.summary: Read back a Lines sheet that mirrors a Banner Grant Inception to Date export (FRIGITD) by formula, one row per code with budget, spent, committed and the account it rolls up to (a formula built from General Accounting's expense code list and the chart of accounts); the pane fills the export's tab name and the sheet fills itself. Nothing written; the checks reported.

assertions.label: every expense code is in the chart the Account formula was built from; a ? in column C names one that is not
at least one row on the Lines sheet

components.name: award-status
components.summary: Read an award's status off an Award status sheet, a template filled from the request (title, sponsor, PI, dates) whose every figure is a formula over a Lines sheet from a FRIGITD export: the award's own accounts listed with budget, spent and committed under each, flags for accounts out of step with the time elapsed, burn rate, runway, the projected spend at the end date, an F&A check on the MTDC base against the overhead posted with the effective rate, the rebudget each account's pace implies with the moves that need the sponsor, the closeout figures, the budget pools as Banner enforces them, and a reconciliation. The skill writes nothing.

assertions.label: budget total found from the Lines sheet (its account rows must carry the budget)

components.name: award-review
components.summary: Award check, award review, check this award: a monthly award review from a Banner Grant Inception to Date export (FRIGITD) opened in Excel, on the tab the request names, else the only tab that looks like the export, else the one the user is on. The award's facts from the export's key block, a Lines sheet that mirrors the export by formula, an Award status sheet (the award's accounts with budget, spent and committed under each, flags, burn rate, runway, projection, F&A check, rebudget at pace, closeout, budget pools) and an email to the PI, facts only. Four steps run by the pane, no question. This is the skill to call for any request to check or review an award.

context.workbook: the Banner Grant Inception to Date export (FRIGITD) is open in this workbook; its key block carries the grant, title, agency, PI and project period
context.frigitd_tab: ? the tab name the request gives for the export, as written; none if it gives none
? the export's tab name alone, as the facts step's Tab line gives it

context.sponsor_award: ? the sponsor and the grant code
context.start_date: ? the start date as the facts step wrote it
context.end_date: ? the end date as the facts step wrote it

context.sender: ? the user's name if the conversation gives it; none if not

components.name: pi-awards
components.summary: List a PI's active awards off a Banner Grant Personnel Inquiry export (FRIPSTG) on the tab the request names or the one found by its headers: one line per award with grant, title, proposal number and maximum amount, then the inactive count. Reading only.

components.name: current-pending
components.summary: Fill a Current and pending sheet, one row per award of a PI: grant and title from the request's list, and, for each award whose FRIGITD export is a tab in the workbook, the sponsor and project period copied from its key block and the total award as a SUM over its budget column; person-months, overlap, role and the sponsor's number left yellow for the PI. Sponsor-neutral, for SciENcv and NIH Other Support alike.

components.name: current-pending-support
components.summary: A PI's current and pending support from Banner exports opened in Excel: the award list from the FRIPSTG export, then a Current and pending sheet with each award's sponsor, period and total from its FRIGITD export where the workbook has one, and the PI's cells left yellow. Two steps run by the pane, no question; the reply names the exports still to fetch.

context.workbook: a Banner Grant Personnel Inquiry export (FRIPSTG) for the PI is open in this workbook, and Grant Inception to Date exports (FRIGITD) for some of the awards may be too
context.fripstg_tab: ? the tab name the request gives for the personnel inquiry export, as written; none if it gives none

context.pi: ? the PI's name as the awards step wrote it
context.awards: ? the awards step's lines for the active awards, one per line, as written

components.name: proposal-workbook
components.summary: Turn a chosen funding opportunity into a proposal-planning workbook: a table of eight steps the pane runs one after another, each skill in its own conversation with a context the pane fills from the run's earlier outputs (ask; RFA sheet; narrative; work plan; a Rates sheet; budget outline; NSF budget form; Gantt). The budget is estimated from the plan and asks nothing; a reviewer edits the outline sheet and reruns the form.

context.opportunity: ? the opportunity the user chose: title, number and grants.gov link as listed in the earlier reply
context.question: Confirm which opportunity this proposal is for. Then ask, in one message, for what only the user knows, each with what will be assumed if they say estimate: the proposal title (assume one from the idea, in the announcement's title format if it has one); the idea in a few sentences (required); the award type or track when the announcement has them; the team as roles and names (assume a PI and one graduate student); the project length and expected start (assume the announcement's maximum). Then ask, open-ended, for other context: a facility, dataset or website to build on, a partner, a prior award, an institutional cap, a reviewer concern, a section to emphasise, and any budget must-haves (a piece of equipment, a partner with a subaward, a named consultant, people who must be on it, cost sharing the sponsor requires), since the budget is estimated from the plan and asks nothing later. Say that the answer starts the build: RFA sheet, narrative, work plan, rates, budget outline, NSF budget form and timeline follow without further questions.
